page_summary:
Selected Stories of Philip K. Dick is the canonical works-table record for PKD's short-story collection corpus item. The record links the archive's preserved manifestation of the work to the broader corpus and gives researchers a single place to follow its bibliographic and interpretive context.

The preserved archive item here is Selected Stories of Philip K. Dick (Unknown).

The source record itself summarizes the work as follows: Selected Stories of Philip K. Dick is a short story anthology. The text excerpt consists primarily of Dick's novel bibliography rather than a story table of contents, spanning his entire career from Solar Lottery through The Transmigration of Timothy Archer.

The bibliography lists all major novels including Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?, The Man in the High Castle, A Scanner Darkly, Ubik, VALIS, Flow My Tears the Policeman Said, The Three Stigmata of Palmer Eldritch, and Deus Irae (co-written with Roger Zelazny). The inclusion of Radio Free Albemuth and The Transmigration of Timothy Archer dates this collection to after 1982.

Dick was one of the most prolific short story writers in science fiction, producing over 120 stories primarily during the 1950s and early 1960s, many of which have been adapted for film and television. This collection draws from that vast output to present a curated selection of his finest shorter works.

The entry is most useful when tracing publication context, later commentary, or relationships to other works.
